scope_note: Evidence-backed changes to how Narrative Systems observes, evaluates, or improves its own behavior. This ledger is process evidence, never research evidence.

entries.title: Speaker labeling learns from corpus-scale turn structure

observation.summary: A 20-excerpt pilot passed its attribution threshold and authorized a 400-source expansion; the expanded derived corpus then exposed repeated same-speaker labels and paragraph boundaries being treated as turns.

diagnosis.summary: The labeler needed to distinguish continuous solo speech from speaker changes and suppress duplicate labels on consecutive blocks by the same explicit speaker.

intervention.summary: The transformation now emits one continuous label for solo sources, carries the last explicit speaker across adjacent blocks, and regenerates affected derived transcripts.

validation.summary: Regression tests exercise continuous solo bodies and consecutive explicit turns by the same speaker.

outcome.summary: The repair was applied across 253 derived files and is regression-protected. A new post-repair human excerpt sample has not yet been recorded.
outcome.measure: 253 derived files regenerated; post-repair manual QA rate pending.

entries.next_measure: Repeat the 20-excerpt human QA sample on repaired output and compare accepted attribution and turn-boundary rates with the pilot.

entries.title: Historical-reference review becomes detector control data

observation.summary: The historical-reference detector produced a review queue containing host-only, wrong-event, and uncertain speaker attributions alongside voice-supported candidates.

diagnosis.summary: Reference matching alone could not safely attribute every occurrence to the routed voice; turn-level review decisions needed to survive regeneration.

intervention.summary: Manual accepted and rejected occurrence decisions became structured inputs to the Freeman index builder; rejected candidates remain auditable but no longer contribute to voice-attributed counts.

validation.summary: Tests preserve the separation among provisional suggestions, confirmed mechanisms, accepted occurrences, and rejected occurrences in the structured ledger.

outcome.summary: Eleven July 24 candidates were reviewed: six accepted and five rejected. Subsequent index generation consumes those decisions and retains rejection lineage.
outcome.measure: 6 accepted and 5 rejected manual turn decisions integrated.

entries.next_measure: Apply the same reviewed-decision path to another voice and compare provisional-attribution and rejection rates.

entries.title: Continuity diagnostics become a bounded repair queue

observation.summary: Repository diagnostics measured repeated narrative framing and surfaced unresolved forecasts, unmapped voice identities, counter-pressure gaps, and missing lineage.

diagnosis.summary: Accumulated archive and synthesis state needed prioritized, bounded attention rather than broad regeneration or an undifferentiated integrity failure.

intervention.summary: Continuity triage, longitudinal accountability, and cadence contracts converted diagnostic state into explicit next actions and executable boundaries.

validation.summary: Continuity and cadence tests exercise deterministic triage and bounded validator results.

outcome.summary: The repository now produces bounded attention queues, but no post-intervention rerun yet demonstrates reduced repetition or closure of the identified continuity gaps.
outcome.measure: Baseline exists; comparable post-intervention measurement pending.

entries.next_measure: Rerun narrative reuse and continuity triage over a later matched window and record which baseline gaps closed, persisted, or worsened.

entries.title: Intake hardening accumulates production lessons

observation.summary: Repeated intake work exposed ambiguous titles and dates, duplicate identity risk, provisional routing, and operator confusion between implementation names and the canonical front door.

diagnosis.summary: Landing needed inspectable provenance and duplicate identity before writes, while the operator-facing command needed one stable route.

intervention.summary: The workflow added read-only preflight receipts, canonical source identities, metadata-basis fields, duplicate stops, and a simplified canonical intake front door.

validation.summary: Intake and smart-intake tests cover preflight metadata, identity duplication, routing, canonical command behavior, stable outcome counters, and terminal-retry aggregation.

outcome.summary: The controls now emit stable counters for warnings, duplicate stops, correction signals, successful landings, failures, and terminal retries. A reconstructed July 27 source-state baseline covers 15 landed sources and one correction-signal source; attempt-level duplicate, failure, and retry metrics remain unavailable until saved receipts exist.
outcome.measure: 15 landed sources, 15 unique identities, and 1 correction-signal source; attempt-level baseline pending.

entries.next_measure: Save JSON receipts for the next bounded intake batch and compare its attempt-level warnings, duplicate stops, failures, and retries with this July 27 source-state baseline.

entries.title: Source-anchor policy becomes a validated synthesis gate

observation.summary: The July 30 run began with one source anchor per transcript, while a proposed hard minimum of 40 anchors risked padding and the first synthesis attempt stopped on template and issue-readiness failures.

diagnosis.summary: Anchor quantity was being treated as a proxy for source coverage and synthesis quality; the workflow needed variable coverage targets plus advisory checks for missing and redundant anchors.

intervention.summary: The synthesis contract adopted one anchor per landed source, 2–3 per major mechanism, a normal 24–30 working range, and a justified exception path for 40; the validator added coverage, redundancy, and high-count warnings.

validation.summary: The July 30 source ledger reconciled 12 manifest rows with 12 anchors and zero anchor-quality warnings; the completed issue then validated with zero daily-run failures and zero warnings.

outcome.summary: The policy was consumed by the same run that generated it: 12 source anchors were retained without padding, the synthesis was expanded to the issue contract, and the final issue passed validation.
outcome.measure: 12 manifest-backed sources, 12 source anchors, 0 anchor-quality warnings, and 0 issue-stage validation failures.

entries.next_measure: Apply the variable-anchor checks to the next two synthesis runs and compare anchor redundancy, issue word-range failures, and post-render validation outcomes.

entries.title: Profile-first verification preserves learning before repository promotion

observation.summary: A narrowly scoped Pape repair became entangled with repeated full-repository verification. The profile itself passed, but slow and unrelated repository failures obscured that result, caused redundant work, and increased operator cognitive load.

diagnosis.summary: Dream coupled local lesson eligibility to a much slower repository-wide gate and did not persist completed phase evidence early enough. A timeout, interruption, unsafe inherited pytest configuration, or moving worktree could therefore conceal successful local verification.

intervention.summary: Cadence now persists schema-v3 handoffs around every verification phase, grants bounded local eligibility after the selected profile passes, and reserves repository eligibility for an explicit cache-aware promotion command. Governed validation preflights an external temporary root, passes pytest basetemp directly, removes inherited PYTEST_ADDOPTS, preserves partial receipts, and reports interruption or failure without erasing completed experiment evidence.

validation.summary: Targeted cadence and runtime tests exercise profile-first persistence, separated eligibility, safe temporary-root handling, cache-aware promotion, moving-state rejection, interruption receipts, and Coffee status distinctions. A stable full promotion passed 892 tests and stored a content-addressed success receipt; the identical next promotion skipped structural validation and pytest on a cache hit.

outcome.summary: A profiled Pape Dream reached durable local eligibility in 7.84 seconds without launching repository validation. After explicit promotion, repository use became eligible; a content-equivalent cached promotion completed in 2.576 validator seconds and 9.495 seconds wall time without rerunning structural validation or pytest.
outcome.measure: Pape profile: 7.84 seconds against a 30-second limit; cache-hit promotion: 2.576 validator seconds and 9.495 wall seconds against a 15-second acceptance threshold; 0 structural or pytest phases rerun on the cache hit.

entries.next_measure: Apply profile-first Dream to the next two eligible cadence episodes and compare local completion time, preserved interruption evidence, repository-promotion frequency, cache-hit rate, and operator correction load.
